I'm thinking through how to approach this.


The target directory confirms the website files are present. Reviewing the prompt reveals the system requires a University Course Registration System with Home, Catalog, Registration, and Student Profile pages. The structure should allow seamless navigation, potentially an SPA or multi-page design with responsive navigation, potentially using data attributes to manage page sections within a single HTML file.


Single-page app with hash-based routing is feasible for navigation. The design will implement a navigation bar for all four pages, updating the URL hash for bookmarking and back-button functionality. Core features include a navigation bar, search, filter functionality, course cards, registration form with validation, and a confirmation modal with a data table for registered courses.


Considering detailed page layouts: Home page with a hero banner, quick stats, quick actions, featured courses, and registration announcements. The Catalog page will feature course cards with search and filter options. Registration page will have a form with validation and a confirmation modal. The Student Profile page will display student information, registered courses, and a schedule visualizer.

The design will be responsive and use a modern, vibrant color palette with accessible, high-contrast readability. Plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript will be used, with all files placed in the specified directory, starting with `index.html`. Sample data will be included for 15-20 courses across various departments.


The catalog page's filter bar will provide extensive course searching and filtering capabilities by department, level, credits, availability, and sort order. The home page will feature a welcoming hero section with key metrics, action buttons, and a calendar widget. A prominent header with a logo and navigation links will be consistently present across all pages.


Catalog course cards will include course code, title, credits, department badge, instructor placeholder, schedule, s

gment, and an optional advisor note, alongside a registration summary with unit limits and tuition estimates. A live data table of registered courses with details like course code, title, department, units, grade option, instructor, schedule, and actions (drop, change grade) will be included.


The student profile page will include a header with basic student information.  Academic progress will be visualized with a progress bar and breakdowns of major requirements, general education, and electives. A weekly visual schedule planner, a registered courses table with print/export, and advisor contact card are planned.  Modal windows will confirm course registration and drops, as well as providing course details and toast notifications for success/error alerts.


Considering visual design: a clean, responsive layout will be implemented using media queries for all screen sizes, including a hamburger menu for smaller devices and scrollable data tables. Animations like smooth transitions, badge designs, shadows, glassmorphism touches, and interactive hover states will enhance user experience, along with weekly timetable grid styling and modal backdrop animations. The course database will include 16 comprehensive courses, and the initial registered courses will populate the data tables and schedule right away.


Functionality will include navigation tab switching based on URL hash changes, supporting hash links for each page section. The catalog will implement real-time text search and multi-criteria filtering with sort options, with course cards and dynamic updates to the registered course data table. Course registration management will handle prerequisites, unit limits, duplicate course checks, and add/drop functionality, including grade changes and a quick registration option by course code. Rendering features include course cards with colored badges, the registered courses data table, and a weekly schedule. Modal management will provide toast notifications, and support mobile menu toggling and print functionality.
